question: A 62-year-old woman diagnosed with arterial hypertension treated with amlodipine 10 mg / day and osteoporosis established on denosumab 60 mg sc every 6 months. Consultation by a clinic of 4 months of evolution, consisting of general syndrome, fever of 38ºC and continuous pain in the right lumbar fossa. The examination shows a positive renal fist. An analytical sample showing leukocytes 14,000 / mm3 without left deviation is requested, with Hb 9 g / dL and a VSG of 82 mm at the first hour. The urinary sediment presents leukocyturia and the urine cytology shows abundant macrophages with a foamy appearance. Point out the most likely diagnosis:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "fever" -> "right lumbar fossa pain" -> "positive renal fist" -> "leukocyturia" -> "abundant foamy macrophages" -> "xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis" -> 85%
CHAIN: "fever" -> "right lumbar fossa pain" -> "positive renal fist" -> "leukocyturia" -> "abundant foamy macrophages" -> "renal tuberculosis" -> 60%
CHAIN: "fever" -> "right lumbar fossa pain" -> "positive renal fist" -> "leukocyturia" -> "abundant foamy macrophages" -> "kidney abscess" -> 50%
CHAIN: "fever" -> "right lumbar fossa pain" -> "positive renal fist" -> "leukocyturia" -> "abundant foamy macrophages" -> "renal adenocarcinoma" -> 40%
analysis: The clinical presentation of the patient, including fever, continuous pain in the right lumbar fossa, leukocyturia, and the presence of abundant foamy macrophages in urine cytology, is suggestive of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. This condition is characterized by chronic inflammation and the presence of lipid-laden macrophages, which appear foamy. The elevated leukocyte count and high erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) further support an inflammatory process. Renal tuberculosis, kidney abscess, and renal adenocarcinoma are less likely given the specific finding of foamy macrophages.
